correctness.rationale: The Fu–Li unit-sphere formula is reduced exactly to a range quotient on the quotient of \(\mathbb R^3\) by constants. Exchange symmetry restricts the scale to \(0<q\le1\); the six relative permutations reduce to four exhaustive cases. Identity and reversal give at most \(1\); transposition and cycle give at most \(\sqrt q(2-q)\), whose squared deficit from \(32/27\) factors as \((8-3q)(3q-2)^2/27\). The explicit pair \(u=(0,1)\), \(v=(1,2/3)\), \(a=\sqrt{2/3}\) attains the bound. The standalone checker verifies the finite bookkeeping and exact arithmetic; the global inequalities are proved analytically.

value.rationale: The affine-regular hexagonal plane is a canonical low-dimensional non-Hilbert model, and \(\operatorname{DR}\) is a recently introduced quantitative Hilbert-deviation invariant. An exact attained value strictly between \(1\) and \(2\) provides a meaningful benchmark beyond the endpoint square/diamond examples. The proof also gives a compact reusable reduction to four permutation geometries, so the result is structural rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
